en.headline: Nine hand-foot-mouth disease outbreaks recorded in first three days of week
en.dek: The Centre for Health Protection said activity has risen sharply, with nine outbreaks involving 24 people since Sunday, mostly in kindergartens and primary schools, and has written to schools.
body: Hand-foot-mouth disease activity in Hong Kong has risen significantly, the Centre for Health Protection said today.
In the first three days of this week the centre recorded nine outbreaks involving 24 people. About 90 per cent of the cases occurred in child-care centres, kindergartens or primary schools.

Monitoring data show outbreaks in institutions and schools rose from eight in the week of 13–19 September to 20 in the week of 4–10 October. The centre has sent letters to schools urging them to watch for the latest situation and to report any outbreaks promptly.

The centre reminded the public to maintain personal and environmental hygiene. Hand-foot-mouth disease is common in children, usually caused by enteroviruses, with peaks typically in May–July and October–December.

zh.headline: 本周首三日錄得9宗手足口病爆發 涉24人
zh.dek: 衞生防護中心指活躍程度顯著上升，本周首三天已錄得九宗爆發個案涉24人，九成在幼兒中心、幼稚園或小學，已向學校發信。
body: 衞生署衞生防護中心今日表示，本港手足口病活躍程度近日顯著上升。
本周首三天中心已錄得九宗爆發個案，涉24人。當中約九成個案在幼兒中心、幼稚園或小學發生。
監測數據顯示，院舍及學校爆發由9月13日至19日一周的八宗，上升至10月4日至10日一周的20宗。中心已向學校發信，呼籲留意最新情況，如有爆發應盡快呈報。
中心提醒市民保持個人及環境衛生。手足口病常見於兒童，多由腸病毒引起，高峰期一般在5至7月及10至12月。
